Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important chase! The umpires and the players of England Women Under-19 are out in the middle and so are the openers for India Women Under-19 - Kamalini G and Trisha Gongadi. Charlotte Lambert has the new ball in hand and is raring to go.
... The Run Chase ...

So, we are halfway into the semi-final and India looks the favourite for now. They have batted well throughout the tournament but can they do under pressure? England have some quality bowlers in their ranks but have to be on the money from the word go. Stay tuned for the chase.

Parunika Sisodia is down for a chat. She starts by saying that her plan was clear and to bowl at the stumps and the ball was skidding through which was good for someone like here. Mentions that she is someone who works more on consistency rather than finding more spin. Adds that there wasn't much pressure on us and they just got off to a good start and says that she is confident that their batters can gun this target.

India Women Under-19 will be over the moon right now! They would have taken this score at the start but it wasn't easy going initially. The seamers were taken to cleaners and so were the spinners early on. They lacked a plan and gave too much width but after the drinks break it was Spinner's day out!  Aayushi Shukla and Parunika Sisodia rolled through the middle order while Vaishnavi Sharma cleaned up the tail. The trio shared 8 wickets and were the main architect of England's downfall.

England Women Under-19 do get close to 115 but what a recovery this is from India's point of view. From 81/3 at the end of the 12th over, England were flying high with Davina Perrin smashing all around the park. She was the mainstay and England were eyeing close to 150 at one stage but once Perrin fell, it was a domino effect for England who nosedived against the Indian spinners and ended well below the par total. Only three players ended with a double-digit score and that tells you the story. England were in a strong position with Davina Perrin and Abigale Norgrove laying a good foundation but similar dismissals and being not able to pick the pace off spinners slowed/stopped their process for a big total.

Just a single to end then and only 3 runs come off the final over. This is pitched up full around off, Tilly Corteen-Coleman comes forward and hits it away wide of mid off for a single. England Women Under-19 finish with 113/8 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings! The India Women Under-19 players can be seen around the boundary rope, raring to get onto the field and then they form a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Jemima Spence and the fiery Davina Perrin to open the innings for England Women Under-19. Shabnam has the new ball in hand and is raring to go as we see just a bit of cloud cover now. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the action but first, the mascots and the officials make their way out to the middle, followed by the two sets of players who will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of England first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Marina Iqbal is pitchside. Starts by saying that it is humid out in the middle and adds that it is a 66-meter hit down the ground. Adds that the surface has a mixture of different soils but it is one of the best. Reckons there is some live grass on the deck which will assist the pacers but with how many wickets the spinners have taken so far, they will be crucial and ends by saying that it should be a good contest between bat and ball.

India Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Kamalini G (WK), Trisha Gongadi, Sanika Chalke, Niki Prasad (C), Ishwari Awasare, Mithila Vinod, Aayushi Shukla, Shabnam, Vaishnavi Sharma, Joshitha V J (In for Bhavika Ahire), Parunika Sisodia (In for Sonam Yadav).

England Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Davina Perrin, Jemima Spence, Trudy Johnson, Abigale Norgrove( C), Charlotte Stubbs, Katie Jones (WK), Prisha Thanawala, Amuruthaa Surenkumar (In for Olivia Brinsden), Charlotte Lambert (In for Eve O'Neill), Tilly Corteen-Coleman, Phoebe Brett.

The skipper of India Women, Niki Prasad says they would have batted first as well but are happy to bowl as they have done well bowling first. Tells they have prepared well and now it's time to execute the plan. Feels everyone are motivated and are looking forward to the game. Informs they have made two changes.

Abigale Norgrove, the captain of England Women says they will bat first as runs on board in the semifinal is the way to go. Adds that the deck looks good and they want to play their way with everyone raring to go. Goes on to informs that they are going with a balanced lineup and reckons 120 would be a good score to put on the board but back their bowlers regardless.
TOSS - ENGLAND have won the toss and will BAT first!

Right then, it is a crunch encounter between two seasoned outfits in the women's game but England Women Under-19 will slightly be the underdogs in this one given India Women Under-19 are the reigning champions and have played like it as well. It should be a fascinating watch, so, don't go anywhere as the toss and team sheets will be up in some time.

England Women Under-19 on the other hand are unbeaten as well but a couple of their Super Six matches were washed out which forced them to finish second in Grop B behind South Africa. They have been able to step up with the bat in crucial encounters and Davina Perrin will be the one to watch out for. Their bowling too has been solid but that middle order with the bat is largely untested and will be the key area they would want to improve on.

India Women Under-19 come into this contest on an unbeaten streak and the reigning champions have simply cruised past their opponents. The pacers have been prolific upfront and the batting has been rock solid as well with Trisha Gongadi even hitting a stellar ton not long ago. The spinners will be key for them as usual and they will look to march ahead into the summit clash and try and defend their title.

Hello and welcome to the second semi-final of the Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup. We are at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia as India Women Under-19 and England Women Under-19 gear up for an epic clash for a spot in the final. Just a few moments ago, South Africa Women Under-19 followed in the footsteps of the senior national team by defeating Australia in the first semi-final and sealed a place in the title clash.
... MATCH DAY ...

So, we have India Women Under-19, who are unbeaten in the tournament so far, taking on England Women Under-19 in the second semi-final. India Women Under-19 has been in phenomenal form, particularly with their batting, which has been consistently impressive throughout the tournament. Their last league-stage match against Scotland was a testament to their dominance, where they posted a massive 208 runs, with Trisha Gongadi starring with a century and 3 wickets. Their bowling unit has also been firing on all cylinders, with every bowler contributing to key dismissals. On the other hand, England Women Under-19 have had a couple of washouts, but have won the remaining games. While they've been performing well as a unit, they're yet to unleash their full potential and completely overwhelm an opponent. Can England Women Under-19 bring their A-game and challenge India's unbeaten run, or will India Women Under-19 continue their dominance and march into the final? We will have our answers soon.
